newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram urges inflation acceptance.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram urges inflation acceptance.

text.p: Indian Finance P. Chidambaram said on Tuesday the country must be prepared to accept an inflation rate, measured by the wholesale price index, of about 6.0 to 7.0 percent.
"We must accept a level of six to seven percent of inflation," Chidambaram told a meeting of economic editors in New Delhi.
"Last year, average inflation was about eight percent," he said.
Year-on-year inflation rate stood at 6.51 percent in the week ending October 19.

A finance ministry statement said: "It is likely that the inflation rate could now peak at about seven percent, after which, by November, we should hope to see deceleration in the growth of prices due to the fresh arrivals of Kharif (winter) crops and agro-raw materials."
